text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police on Tuesday mounted road-blocks in Machinga district, more than 100km north east of Blantyre, to check main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) who had allegedly planned to ferry supporters from Lilongwe, more than 200km away in central Malawi, to vote in a by-election.

- The fate of the National Assembly, which faces a boycott from the country's two opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) parties is expected to be decided on December 9, a day set for sitting after it failed in October.
- There are reports of a split in the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party in Blantyre after discontent on the choice of candidate for the postponed by-election.

- Malawi Congress Party (MCP) vice president Gwanda Chakuamba said Malawi may face serious food shortages next year due to limited access to farm resources such as fertilizers and maize seed by smallholder farmers
- Staff at the 109-year-old building for the district commissioner's office in Blantyre on Friday vacated their offices fearing that the building may collapse.
